newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session weaker.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended slightly lower in light dealings Thursday, as the market consolidated after steep gains on Wednesday, traders said.
"It was a little overdone yesterday," one trader said.
Traders said speculative liquidation off of Wednesday's rally pressured values, but failed to gather enough momentum to breach $1,352 a tonne support in the December contract.
Benchmark December cocoa settled down $7 a tonne, at $1,355, after ranging between $1,366 and $1,352. March fell $5 to $1,389, while the rest ended $9 weaker to $1 firmer.
On the charts, traders said the December contract would need to trade above 1,370 to attract substantial buying interest.
They said that the market's fundamental outlook remained a bit bearish, with improved 1996/97 Ivorian crop prospects expected to continue to weigh on prices.
Volume was exceedingly thin, at an estimated 3,258 lots.
